note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 226, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: BAV I CORPS remains explicitly Bavarian and local; derived Germany is not a valid reason to rename it Imperial German in1870.

The Coulmiers municipality explicitly identifies the republican government’s Army of the Loire under d’Aurelle, including line troops, departmental mobiles and francs-tireurs. Only a line-infantry component is represented; the model does not identify or standardize the uniforms and weapons of the mobiles, francs-tireurs or other branches. The kepi, blue-grey campaign capote, garance trousers and Chassepot M1866 with sabre bayonet are a documented 1870 line-infantry analogy. Clothing, regiment, supply and branch varied; this is not a claim that every soldier of the mixed army wore or carried these items. Zouaves, tirailleurs, guards, mobiles, cavalry and artillery are not converted into line infantry. No component proportion, new participant, strength, loss or death is inferred. The Draner print used for visual corroboration was published in 1871; it is not dated to the battle and does not broaden the profile’s eligibility.
